_about: The dated numbers the AI 2027 scenario (Kokotajlo, Alexander, Larsen, Lifland, Dean; April 2025) commits to, from the tables of its compute forecast supplement (Romeo Dean), read from the page on 2026-11-13. Used by the Tensions check server/tensions/checks/ai-2027.js to set the scenario's path beside what has been filed and disclosed. Each series is keyed by calendar year, exactly as the table gives it; nothing here is interpolated or estimated (the check does that, and says so). The scenario is one fast-takeoff story, and its 'leading AI company' is fictional: the check compares it with whichever real lab is furthest along. The site's side panels round some of these differently; only the supplement's tables are used.

leadCompute.label: Leading AI company, annual compute cost

tcoPerH100e.label: Total cost of ownership per H100-equivalent

stockH100e.label: AI-relevant compute in existence, year end

chipsProduced.label: AI chips produced in the year

leadComputeUsed.label: Leading AI company, average compute in use

externalDeploymentShare.label: Leading AI company, share of compute serving customers
externalDeploymentShare.locator: Section 3 table, External deployment (2027 is its first quarter; the table falls to 13% by the fourth)

narrative.claim: The stock market has gone up 30% in 2026

notGradable: The stock of compute (40 million H100-equivalents by the end of 2026) and world AI power (29 GW): nobody publishes a count.
The AI R&D progress multiplier (1.5× in early 2026, 10× by mid-2027): the labs do not disclose one.
How the leading lab splits its compute between research and customers, beyond the one filed figure.
